gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words in solid, even blocks. Megrim is the angular showpiece, its bars and stems cut to the same measured weight, while the body sans does the quiet work of keeping text open and easy to follow.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-aldrich: Storybook charm meets a stiff, techy backbone. Mystery Quest lets its open-jawed curves and compact ascenders do the nostalgic talking up top, while Aldrich follows with tall, cupped letters of a single line width, so the page moves from old tale to modern tidy.
gen-nixie-one-gf-orbit: Thin retro-tech lines, curves left politely open. Nixie One is at its best as a wistful, wire-fine heading with gaps in its curves, whereas Orbit does its job in text, each character standing apart in a sans-serif of rope-like consistency.
